tasks.short: Determine dental product design from prescriptions and actual models

steps.what: Locate the correct prescription or specification and matching model or impression for the laboratory case
inputs: prescriber-issued prescription with case id and revision
laboratory intake case index and labelled model or impression
outputs: matched case prescription and model reference

steps.what: Read and interpret prescriptions or specifications for the dental product to be constructed
inputs: matched case prescription and model reference

steps.what: Examine the actual models or impressions and assess their relevance and adequacy for the prescribed product
inputs: matched case prescription and model reference
technician-understood prescription requirements and ambiguities
actual model or impression

steps.what: Determine the design of the dental product to be constructed and identify unresolved prescription or model issues
inputs: technician-understood prescription requirements and ambiguities
actual model findings and limitations
outputs: technician-formed product design choices and unresolved issues

steps.what: Enter the determined design choices and unresolved issues in the existing laboratory case specification
inputs: technician-formed product design choices and unresolved issues
matched case prescription and model reference

steps.what: Check the final case design specification against the actual prescription and findings and approve its record version
inputs: complete draft case design specification
technician-understood prescription requirements and ambiguities
actual model findings and limitations

steps.what: Save the approved case design specification in the same laboratory case record
inputs: approved case design specification v1

tasks.design: Configure a case-linked prescription view and design-specification form in the {OPS_SYSTEM}. The technician interprets the prescription, examines actual models and determines the design; the form reuses verified case identifiers while the technician records new choices and approves the final specification.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding matching case material and repeating known identifiers can add work around the actual design judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Native case links and prefilled fields can reduce navigation and copying without interpreting clinical instructions.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous prescriptions and inadequate impressions cannot be resolved by copying a template.
tasks.human_edge: Judge what the physical model supports and recognise when a design decision needs clarification.

ambition.what: No new clinical or product-design authority is assumed.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-4 for case and prescription access; review permitted patient-data fields

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: laboratory case systems can link prescriptions and model references and reuse verified identifiers in specification forms.

assumptions: Boundary includes prescription reading, actual model examination, determining design and its existing case specification. Construction, CAD shape creation and obtaining a new prescription are separate work; no saving is claimed for them.

The prescriber supplies case id, revision and instructions; intake staff supplies the labelled physical model reference. s1 checks the match manually, and s2 retains all interpretation. Missing identifiers remain manual exceptions rather than free extraction.

s5 counts actual capture of new design choices and unresolved issues; prefill reuses only case id, prescription version and model reference. Native configuration first; no model invents design details.

Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. The scenario assumes the existing case specification is already part of design work; if absent, do not add it merely to claim saving.
Same-system save takes approximately no effort and stays fully retained. The approved record is not an automatic production-release instruction; any later release needs its own gate.
unknowns: Existing case links and specification entry process
Proportion of physical versus digital models
research_questions: Can the technician find and verify one prescription/model pair without extra navigation?
Does prefill remove only repeated identifiers while preserving all actual design capture?

already_counted.description: Capture and check actual design choices and exceptions

incremental.description: Maintain case-link and specification form mappings

approvals.approved_version: approved case design specification v1; edits require s6 again

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 8 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 7.5. High allows 2.5 extra hours resolving case-link exceptions; low applies when native case links and form prefill already exist.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Train and supervise dental laboratory bench work

steps.what: Find the current procedure and training objective for the dental technician or bench worker's task
inputs: procedure-owner approved procedure version
training-owner objective and existing trainee or course reference
outputs: checked current demonstration and supervision reference

steps.what: Train other dental technicians or dental laboratory bench workers through demonstration and explanation
inputs: checked current demonstration and supervision reference
actual trainee and bench work
outputs: actual demonstration delivered and trainee questions

steps.what: Supervise actual dental laboratory work and observe technique, understanding and needed corrections
inputs: actual demonstration delivered and trainee questions
actual trainee or bench-worker performance
outputs: actual observed technique and supervision findings

steps.what: Give feedback, correct misunderstandings and agree any further practice with the worker
inputs: actual observed technique and supervision findings
actual trainee responses
outputs: actual feedback and agreed further practice

steps.what: Record actual training delivered, observed findings and further practice in the existing training record
inputs: actual demonstration delivered and trainee questions
actual observed technique and supervision findings
actual feedback and agreed further practice
training-owner objective and existing trainee or course reference
outputs: complete actual training and supervision record

steps.what: Check actual findings and approve the final training record without inferring competence from attendance
inputs: complete actual training and supervision record

steps.what: Save the approved actual training and supervision record in the same learning system
inputs: approved actual training record v1
outputs: stored actual training and supervision record

tasks.design: Configure current-procedure links in the {DOCS} and reuse existing trainee and course identifiers in the {LMS}. Demonstration, observation and feedback remain human; only after they occur does the technician record actual findings and approve the final learning record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding current procedures and repeating known training identifiers can add work around practical instruction.
tasks.enabler_now: Native links and form prefill can reuse approved references without judging a worker's technique.
tasks.still_hard: Hands-on skill and safe technique need direct observation and tailored feedback.
tasks.human_edge: Notice subtle technique errors and adapt the explanation to the learner.

ambition.what: No additional assessment authority or new service is assumed.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-4 for training access and staff consultation if observation records change

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: learning systems can reuse trainee and course metadata while trainers enter actual completion and observation findings.

assumptions: Boundary includes practical training, supervision, feedback and the existing actual training record. Worker practice time is outside the focal denominator and receives no saving.

Procedure owners supply id, current version and approval status; training owners supply objective and trainee/course identifiers. Missing metadata is checked manually in s1. No attendance, competence or observation record exists merely because a session was planned.

s5 occurs after demonstration, observation and feedback and retains 4.8 hours for actual capture and correction. Only repeated identifiers are prefilled; no transcript or automatic skill assessment is assumed.

Native configuration first. Shares and reductions are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. Where no formal training record exists, remove that scenario component and remeasure rather than inventing paperwork savings.
Same-system save remains fully retained. No automatic completion notification or certification is proposed.
unknowns: Whether a formal training record is already kept
Current procedure version controls and learning-system links
research_questions: Can a trainer find the applicable current procedure quickly?
Does prefill preserve the distinction between delivered training and demonstrated competence?

already_counted.description: Capture and check actual observations and follow-up practice

incremental.description: Maintain procedure links and training form identifiers

approvals.approved_version: approved actual training record v1; edits require s6 again

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross 6.2 minus 0.5 upkeep gives 5.7. High allows 1.7 additional hours checking outdated references or identifiers; low applies when existing native links and prefill already cover the work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The technician spends less time locating case or procedure references and repeating identifiers, while product-design judgement and practical training remain central.
skills_to_grow: Distinguish delivered training from observed competence
role.ambitious_version: Use clear case and procedure references to support careful design decisions and individual practical instruction.
